News


October 28, 2026


Amber Wesdorp


**DENVER, Colorado – October 28, 2026 –** Starcloud, an orbital data center developer, and Quindar, a mission operations software provider, announced a strategic partnership to bring data center–grade reliability to compute and mission operations on orbit. Together, Starcloud and Quindar provide commercial and government partners a path to process mission data and make operational decisions on-orbit, even through denied or degraded environments.


Under the partnership, Quindar will deploy and operate its cloud-native mission management platform onboard Starcloud’s constellation of compute satellites, extending the cloud into space. This introduces a new generation of mission operations: a complete solution running on orbital infrastructure, across a combination of terrestrial and orbital cloud regions. Running Quindar in orbit will validate three capabilities: resilience across terrestrial and space data center regions, mission data processing at the edge, and real-time decisions to maintain spacecraft bus uptime.


Together, these capabilities extend Quindar’s “Lights Out, Always On” approach into orbit. By bringing Quindar’s automation directly onboard, Starcloud’s orbital data centers can execute mission workflows and respond to changing conditions autonomously while utilizing the reliability that on-orbit computing provides.


Using Starcloud’s data centers in space, Starcloud-1 and Starcloud-2, Quindar will provide telemetry and operational insights to help demonstrate performance in orbit and support fleet expansion. With data to support its growth, Starcloud can focus on scaling the hardware and compute services that commercial and government missions depend on.


**Cloud expectations, orbital environment, mission grade reliability**


Government missions and commercial partners depend on cloud infrastructure that delivers continuous, reliable service, wherever it runs, even when the data center is moving through orbit. Delivering that experience in space means managing link scheduling, spectrum rules, and orbital maneuvers alongside the compute itself. Starcloud brings the infrastructure; Quindar brings the operations software. The companies will work toward terrestrial data center reliability in an orbital environment. Together, they are building the foundation for a new layer of government infrastructure in space and the dependable service commercial customers demand.


Philip Johnston, CEO, Starcloud, said, “Our orbital Compute Layer enables customers to collect, analyze, and act on orbit without requiring a round-trip to the ground. Quindar provides us with a proven operations platform that government users trust. This partnership allows us to focus on delivering the full value of our Compute Layer to the warfighter, closing decision-action timelines faster than ever before.”


“Government partners using Quindar to operate their satellites now have a PACE plan for C2 – a service that runs in orbit on Starcloud even when ground stations are disrupted.” said Nate Hamet, CEO, Quindar. “Starcloud’s compute lets our software make uptime decisions on orbit in real time, and our platform gives their fleet the operations backbone to stay up. Together, we’re designed to raise uptime and resilience for customers who can’t afford downtime.”


**About Starcloud**
Starcloud is building America’s Sovereign Compute Layer in orbit.


**About Quindar**
Quindar is a mission management service for modern space operations. Its five integrated products — Portal, Event, Control, Plan, and Flight — provide mission teams with a common operating picture across spacecraft, payloads, ground networks, and operational stakeholders. Built for commercial, civil, and national security missions, Quindar delivers secure, resilient, and automation-first operations. For more information, visit www.quindar.space.
